transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for having me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. Um... well, I suppose occupational health actually sent me. I really don't want to make a fuss, but they noticed I've gotten into this... sort of pattern lately. 

I'm a biological scientist, and I just tend to push breakfast and lunch aside when things get busy during my lab runs or, you know, exhibition work. It's just so easy to lose track of time when you're focused. And then, by the time I actually do sit down to eat, I just prefer to keep it to something very small and... well, controlled. Just so I don't feel sluggish, you know? It's really mostly a scheduling thing, I think, but they wanted me to speak with you to be safe. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you find yourself wanting to eat when you do take a break?

Um, well... not exactly? I mean, I know I probably *should* want to eat, but... I just don't really feel hungry. 

When I take a break, I'm usually just thinking about the next step in the experiment, or I'm just enjoying the moment to sit down and rest my feet. I don't really get those hunger pangs that other people talk about. Or if I do, I guess I'm just so used to working through them that I don't really notice them anymore. 

It's actually quite convenient, really, because it means I don't get distracted by cravings or anything. But... I suppose that's probably not the right way to look at it, is it? I mean, I know you're supposed to eat regularly. Am I making it sound worse than it is? I just... I really don't feel the urge to eat very often. Is that... is that very unusual?
Do you ever think about your weight when you're deciding what or how much to eat?

Um, well... I mean, I suppose it crosses my mind, yes. I hope that doesn't sound too vain or anything. I just... I like to keep things consistent. 

I guess I do weigh myself, and... well, to be perfectly honest, if the scale goes up even a fraction, I get this... this sort of sharp panic. Like I'm losing the discipline I've worked so hard to maintain. It's silly, I know, because intellectually I understand that weight fluctuates, but... it just feels like a failure on my part if I let it slip. 

I try not to let it dictate everything, but it definitely plays a role in... in keeping my portions small. Is that... is that something you hear a lot from people? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you think you would eat more if you didn't worry about gaining weight?

Oh, um... that's an interesting question. I'm not really sure, to be honest. 

I suppose... maybe? But honestly, I think it's just so ingrained in me now to eat the way I do, you know? It's just how my routine is set up. I don't think I'd suddenly start eating huge meals even if the weight thing wasn't in the back of my mind, just because my body isn't really used to it anymore. 

I'm sorry, I don't know if that's a very helpful answer. It's just hard to separate the two things in my head at this point. I hope I'm not being difficult by not having a clear "yes" or "no" for you... does that make sense, though?
Do you feel like your eating habits would change if you weren't worried about gaining weight?

Oh, I'm so sorry, I know you just asked me essentially the same thing. I must not have given you a very clear answer a moment ago, I really apologize for that. 

Um... to be completely honest, I really just don't know. I'd like to think that if that worry was completely gone, I might be a little more... relaxed about my meals? But I just can't quite picture it. It's almost like trying to design an experiment without a control variable—it just doesn't quite compute in my head right now. 

I hope it's alright that I don't have a more definitive answer for you? I feel terrible that I can't give you a straightforward yes or no. I really am trying to think it through, I just... I'm really not sure. Is it normal to struggle this much with a hypothetical question like that?
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is the main reason you eat so little?

Oh, I see... well, yes. I suppose it really must be. 

Like I mentioned a few minutes ago, just seeing the scale go up even a tiny fraction sets off that... that really sharp panic in me. That awful feeling that I'm completely losing all the discipline I've worked so incredibly hard to maintain. So, if I'm being completely honest with you—and I really am trying to be—that fear of the number going up probably is the main thing keeping my portions so small. 

I'm so sorry it took me a few tries to just give you a straight answer about that. I think I try to convince myself it's just about being healthy or sticking to a routine, so I don't sound too... well, irrational, I suppose. I just want to make sure I'm explaining it accurately so I don't waste your time. Does that answer your question a bit better?
Do you think you would be happy with your weight if you were a few pounds heavier than you are now?

Oh, gosh... um. I really want to give you a good answer for that, I really do. I know the... well, the right answer is probably that I should be perfectly fine with it, or that a few pounds shouldn't matter at all. But honestly? I'm just not sure. 

I try to look at it logically. You know, with my background in biology, I know a few pounds is just a normal fluctuation in any system. But when I actually try to picture myself being heavier than I am right now... my mind just kind of blanks. I really don't know if "happy" is the word I could use. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm being so unhelpful today with all these vague answers. I just really can't say for sure how I would feel. I hope that's an okay answer? I really am trying to be as honest as I can with you, I just don't want to tell you the wrong thing.
Do you think you would still want to restrict your food intake if you weren't afraid of gaining weight?

Oh, um... wow, that's another really tough one to picture. I'm sorry, I feel like I'm just repeating myself today, aren't I? I really hope I'm not being frustrating to work with.

If I wasn't afraid of gaining weight... would I still restrict? I mean... I honestly don't know. I'd like to say no, that I'd just eat normally like everyone else. But... well, I've had this routine for so long now. It's almost comforting, in a way? Like a very structured protocol in the lab. I know exactly what to expect. 

So maybe I still would, just out of habit or because it feels... safe? Or maybe I wouldn't. I'm so sorry, I know that's such a wishy-washy answer. I just genuinely can't untangle the fear of the weight from the actual habit of eating this way right now. Is it okay that I don't have a clear yes or no for you on that? I really am trying to give you the most accurate information I can.
Do you think there's anything else, besides the fear of gaining weight, that contributes to your decision to restrict your food intake?

Oh, gosh. Um... besides the fear of gaining weight? I really want to make sure I'm answering this right for you. 

I suppose... well, I really don't think there's anything else. I mean, I try to keep things very logical, and I can't really think of any other major reason why I would keep my portions so small. I don't want to overcomplicate things or give you information that isn't useful. 

I'm so sorry if that's not what you were looking for. I just really haven't noticed anything else driving it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful.
Do you think being thin is important to you?

Oh, um... important? I... I want to give you a good answer here. I know you're asking about being thin, but... well, to be completely honest—and I hope this doesn't sound too silly or vain—I don't really see myself as thin at all. 

When I look in the mirror in the mornings before I head into the lab, I mostly just notice my stomach, or my hips. And... well, seeing them just makes me feel like I look careless? Or maybe unserious. In my line of work, discipline and precision are everything, and I just worry that looking that way makes me seem sloppy or unprofessional. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds a bit irrational. I just don't want you to think I'm overly obsessed with my appearance, it's more about wanting to look put-together. Does that answer what you were asking? I really hope I'm not going too far off track for you today.
Do you think you would still feel the need to restrict your food intake if you felt you looked thin?

Oh, um... wow. That's... I'm sorry, I feel like I'm really struggling with these hypothetical questions today. I really want to give you a solid answer. 

If I actually felt like I looked thin... I honestly don't know what I would do. I think... well, I'd like to believe that if I finally reached a point where I looked completely put-together and, you know, acceptable, I wouldn't need to be so strict with my meals anymore. But because I really don't feel that way right now, it's just so hard to even imagine being in that headspace. 

I'm so sorry, I know "I don't know" isn't very helpful for your notes. I just don't want to guess and give you misleading data. Is it alright if I leave that as a maybe? I really am trying my best to answer these properly for you, I promise.
Do you think you would still feel anxious or panicked if you gained a small amount of weight, even if you weren't restricting your food intake?

Oh, gosh... um... I really want to make sure I'm understanding you correctly. So, if I wasn't restricting, but I gained a little weight... would I still panic? 

I... well, to be completely honest with you, and I hope this doesn't make me sound too extreme or... or difficult... but yes, I think I would. Even just thinking about it makes me a little tense. 

It's just that... well, when I step on the scale, if the number goes up even just a fraction of a pound, I get this... this really sharp feeling of panic. It's not just about the number, I promise. It's more that it feels like I'm losing my grip on things? Like all the discipline and structure I've worked so incredibly hard to maintain is just slipping away, and I'm letting myself become careless again. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds like such an overreaction for a grown woman. I just really want to be transparent with you so you have all the right information. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not coming across as too neurotic about it.
Do you feel like you would lose control if you weren't restricting your food intake?

Oh, um... lose control? That's... I want to make sure I'm answering this the right way. 

I guess... well, "lose control" sounds so dramatic, doesn't it? I don't think I'd completely fall apart or anything like that. I like to think I'm a fairly rational person, especially with my background in science. But... I suppose if I didn't have my meal plans and my routines... I might feel a little bit... unmoored? 

It's just that having a schedule for what I eat helps me stay focused for work. Without it, I might just feel a bit disorganized, maybe? Not totally out of control, just... less efficient. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm talking in circles. I just want to give you a good answer without making it sound like I'm totally unhinged. Does that sound like what you were asking about? I really hope I'm being helpful.
Do you think you restrict your food intake more because you want to be thin or because you're afraid of losing control over your eating?

Oh, that’s a really insightful question. I... I want to give you a clear answer, but it’s actually quite hard to separate the two in my head. I guess I’ve never really stopped to analyze which one is the primary... driver. 

If I had to guess, I honestly don't know which one outweighs the other. I mean, wanting to look neat and, you know, thin, is definitely part of it, because it just makes me feel more presentable and professional. But the control aspect... keeping my routine tight just helps me function better at work and in the lab. 

I'm so sorry, I wish I could give you a more definitive answer. They just sort of blend together for me into one general feeling of... needing structure, I suppose? I really hope it's okay if I say it's a mix of both, or that I'm just not entirely sure. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you think you would restrict your food intake if you didn't feel like it helped you maintain control over your life?

Oh, um... that's... gosh, that's another really good question. I want to make sure I'm giving you a helpful answer here. 

If it didn't help me feel... structured, or in control? I... I don't really know, to be perfectly honest. I've been doing things this way for so long that it's hard to imagine what it would be like if that piece of it was just... gone. 

I suppose... well, maybe I wouldn't be quite as strict about it? But I honestly couldn't say for sure. I hope that's an okay answer... I'm so sorry I don't have a better hypothetical for you. I just really want to be accurate and not just guess at something I haven't experienced. Does that make sense?
Do you think your desire to maintain control over your eating is stronger than your fear of gaining weight?

Oh, um... wow, you're really asking the tough ones today, aren't you? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right perspective on this... 

I think... well, it's hard to pull them apart, really. But if I'm being completely honest—and I do want to be a good patient and give you the whole picture—the weight part is... it's quite significant. 

I don't want to sound vain or superficial, because I know as a scientist I should be focused on health and data, not just... appearance. But honestly, if I step on the scale and it goes up, even just a tiny fraction of a pound... I get this sudden, sharp feeling of panic. It's like... it feels like all the discipline and hard work I've put into maintaining my routine is just slipping away. 

So I guess the fear of the number going up is very tied to that feeling of losing my discipline. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds a bit silly or irrational for someone my age. Does that answer what you were asking? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for your notes.
Do you think your restrictive eating is more about avoiding weight gain or about maintaining a sense of control over your daily life?

Oh, um... I feel like I'm repeating myself a bit, and I really don't want to frustrate you or seem like I'm not trying to answer your questions properly. I want to be helpful, I really do.

It's just... they are so incredibly intertwined for me. Avoiding the weight gain and keeping that structure... it's almost like they are the exact same thing in my mind? Like, if my weight stays exactly where I want it, then I know my daily routine is working, and I feel calm and in control. And if I stick to my routine perfectly, then I know I won't gain weight. 

I don't know if I can honestly say one is *more* important than the other. I'm really sorry, I know you're trying to get a clear picture of my motivations, and I feel bad that I can't just give you a simple 'A or B' answer. Is it alright if I just say they work together? I hope I'm not being too difficult.
Do you think you would still restrict your food intake if you knew you couldn't gain weight no matter what you ate?

Oh... goodness. That's a fascinating question. Um... I suppose as a biologist, my brain sort of trips up a little on the premise of, you know, physical intake not having any biological effect at all. But... if I try to just imagine that scenario... I honestly don't know what I would do. 

I really wish I could give you a definitive 'yes' or 'no' so you could have a clear answer for your assessment. I just... I've never lived in a reality where I didn't have to worry about the physical consequences of what I eat, so it's incredibly hard to predict how I would behave. I might still need the structure of my meals just to feel grounded, or... maybe I would finally just let go a little bit? 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just guessing at this point, and I don't want to give you inaccurate data. I hope it's alright with you that I don't have a better answer for that one? I promise I'm really trying to think it through for you.
Do you think your restrictive eating is primarily driven by a fear of gaining weight or by a need to feel in control of your daily life?

Oh, dear... um, I feel terrible, because I know you've essentially just asked me this, and I really, really don't want to come across as evasive or uncooperative. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult. 

I genuinely just... I don't think I can pick one as the primary driver. I've been trying to analyze it in my head while we've been talking, trying to figure out which one is the root cause for you, but... they just feel like two sides of the exact same coin. 

I know you're trying to get to the bottom of this, and I really wish I could just hand you the exact data point you need. I'm so sorry I keep giving you these fuzzy answers. Is it okay if we just say it's an equal mix? I hope I'm not messing up your assessment by not being able to choose one over the other.
Do you think you would still feel the need to restrict your food intake if you felt completely in control of other aspects of your life?

Oh, wow... um... that's another really good question. You're very thorough, and I really appreciate how carefully you're looking at all of this. 

Um... if I felt completely in control of everything else... I mean, I'd like to think I wouldn't need to be so rigid with my meals. It sounds lovely, honestly, to just have everything else perfectly managed and not have to worry about my food as much. 

But... I'm just not entirely sure. Life is so unpredictable, you know? There's always a grant deadline, or an experiment that doesn't go right, or... just life things. So it's hard to imagine a scenario where I feel perfectly in control of everything. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm failing at giving you a straightforward answer again. I really want to be helpful. Do you think it's normal to not know the answer to that? I hope I'm making at least a little bit of sense.
